author: Russell Brand
description:
At 28, Dr. Eric Berg says his health had reached a breaking point. He describes dealing with arthritis, digestive problems, pre-diabetes, kidney stones and osteoporosis while living largely on junk food. Eventually, he began changing what he ate, cutting back on carbohydrates and focusing more heavily on protein.

What began as an attempt to pull himself out of poor health eventually became an obsession with understanding nutrition and the body — something Dr. Berg says he has continued studying for decades. He also reflects on his old eating habits, including constant snacking and nightly ice cream, and how difficult it was for him to stop once he started.

Now 61, Dr. Berg says he lives a very healthy lifestyle and believes that if he had never become sick in the first place, he probably wouldn’t be where he is today.

author: Russell Brand
description:
Russell and his guest begin with a story about being warned away from Scientology — and how that warning only made it more tempting to investigate. The conversation then turns toward Christianity and whether there were parts of the faith that were initially difficult to accept.

Russell says his own life had conditioned him to resist Christ until a personal moment of crisis changed that relationship entirely. From there, he argues that modern culture has normalized behaviors and values that would once have seemed extreme, while openly talking about Jesus or faith is often treated as embarrassing, irrational, or strange.

The result is a provocative question: how did faith become the thing that feels culturally rebellious?

author: Russell Brand
description:
Russell’s guest Sonia Elijah examines the Center for Countering Digital Hate, a British-American NGO that she argues has played a major role in efforts to restrict online dissent. She discusses the group’s 2021 Disinformation Dozen report, which claimed that twelve individuals — including RFK Jr. — were responsible for a large share of anti-vaccine content circulating online.

Elijah then points to leaked internal documents that, according to reporting she cites, identified weakening Elon Musk’s X/Twitter as a strategic priority, including through pressure on advertisers and coordinated boycott campaigns. The conversation explores the relationship between advocacy groups, government officials, tech platforms, and advertisers — and raises broader questions about who ultimately decides which voices are amplified or suppressed online.

author: Russell Brand
description:
Russell and his guest argue that each of us is living through our own version of the Garden of Eden right now, whether we recognize it or not. The serpent’s temptation, they suggest, wasn’t a one-time event — it keeps repeating in the mind through whatever personally draws our attention and desire.

From there, the conversation turns to the cost of truly walking with God: obedience, discipline, and resisting the constant pull away from Him. They make the broader claim that modern culture itself often functions as that temptation, continually directing us toward distraction, desire, and attachment.

A thought-provoking reframing of the Garden of Eden as an ongoing inner struggle — and of what it really means to remain close to God.
